rows.b: A suffix forming adjectives, a variant of -ic, as in theatric.
How many requests an API allows per minute — a non-issue when the model lives on your device.
Deliberately attacking a model with tricky prompts to find its failure and safety holes before the public does.
Re-running old evaluations after each change to make sure nothing that worked got broken.
Any technique, like dropout or weight decay, that discourages overfitting and keeps the model general.
An activation that passes positive numbers through unchanged and turns negatives to zero — simple and fast.
A setting that lowers the score of tokens already used, discouraging the model from repeating itself.
A shortcut that adds a block's input to its output, letting gradients flow cleanly through very deep networks.
Storing answers to repeated questions so identical prompts return instantly.
Reinforcement learning from human feedback: training a model to prefer the answers humans rate highest.
A lighter cousin of layer normalization that rescales by the root-mean-square, skipping the mean subtraction.
How well the model holds up on odd, adversarial, or out-of-distribution inputs.
Telling the model who to be, like a tutor or a pirate, to shape its voice and behavior.
Switching back to the previous model version when a new one misbehaves.
A way of encoding word position by rotating the query and key vectors, which handles long sequences gracefully.
A summarization score measuring overlap between the model's summary and human-written ones.
The tiny network in a mixture-of-experts model that picks which experts handle each token.
The environment executing the model, whether a browser, a phone, or a server.
